narrative: OMX30 faces a bullish macro backdrop with strong continental Europe momentum (+2.0% average) and falling US rates (10Y at 4.848%, down 114bps) reducing DCF discount rates. Commodity rally—gold +1.76%, copper +2.33%—fuels mining (Boliden) and industrial cyclicals, while weakening USD/SEK (10.22, -0.23%) enhances export competitiveness. However, weak ADX (8.7) and MACD below signal introduce technical caution; the index sits only +2.5% above 200-MA and -0.4% below 50-MA, suggesting consolidation bias. Oil weakness (-3.31%) provides consumer tailwind but pressures industrial input costs—a conflicting signal. OMX30 likely opens +0.6% to +1.0%, tracking European strength into US data.
morningBrief: European equity momentum is running hot this morning—DAX, CAC, FTSE all north of +1.7%—and OMX30 should track higher into the open, likely +0.7% to +1.0%. Key support sits at 3085 (lower Bollinger band); resistance at 3180 (50-MA). ADX is weak (8.7, 30% confidence haircut applied), so don't chase hard; expect chop. Commodity tailwind benefits Boliden (copper/gold rally), while weakening USD/SEK is a gift to exporters—watch Volvo B, Atlas Copco A, Ericsson B for breakout momentum. Banks (SEB A, Handelsbanken A) are mixed: yields down is margin pressure, but risk sentiment improving supports valuations. Oil weakness (-3.31%) is a minor consumer positive but watch energy input costs for industrials. US Jobless Claims at 14:30 CET is the day's key catalyst; a beat could extend the rally, a miss could reverse it. Play the long side of Boliden and select industrials; stay tactical on financials until rate picture clears.
